# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Denial of Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)**
**Member:** Riley Brooks
**Member ID:** W997409334
**Date of Notice:** 2026-08-09
**Reference Number:** POC-AA9EA32E7D-95281
**Governing Policy:** Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy (https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf), Original Effective 6/9/21; Revision 6/9/21

Dear Molina Healthcare Appeals Department,

I am writing to request reconsideration of the denial of my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), which I received notice of on 2026-08-09. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in your possession show that the reason given for the denial — inadequate conservative treatment — does not match what actually happened in my care.

## The Reason for Denial

Your notice states: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

## What Your Own Policy Requires, and What My Records Show

Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 states, regarding diagnostic arthroscopy, that it "may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> " Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

My records show that I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest, and that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side. This is a documented loss of function that interferes with my daily activities.

The policy also states:

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My records document more than three months of non-surgical treatment: 12 weeks (16 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics from 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-24, six months of NSAID use with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19 that gave only four weeks of partial relief. That is three separate conservative treatment modalities, each documented, over a period well beyond three months.

The policy further states:

> "and  Demonstration of functionally limited range of motion (active or passive) on physical examination as compared to the non-involved side  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration, including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My physical exam findings document that my range of motion is limited by pain and that provocative testing on the affected side was positive. I am asking Molina to confirm in writing whether these exam findings, together with the MRI showing a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy (2026-06-16), were considered, since the imaging and exam findings directly support the loss-of-function and physical-examination elements of your own criteria.

I note that the policy excerpts provided to me for this appeal do not include a section specifically labeled for rotator cuff repair (as opposed to diagnostic arthroscopy, debridement, labral repair, or other listed procedures). If Molina applied criteria specific to rotator cuff repair beyond what is quoted above, I have not yet been given that specific language, which is part of what I am requesting below.

## Request for the Criteria Applied to My Determination

Molina's own utilization-management materials state that clinical review criteria are MCG guidelines available behind the secure provider portal, and that members may call to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the MCG guideline title and the specific criteria applied to my determination**, so that I and my surgeon can review exactly what standard was used to deny this request.

## What I Am Asking

I am asking Molina to reconsider this denial in light of the conservative treatment already documented in my chart — physical therapy, NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection, all within the twelve months before my surgeon requested surgery — and to provide the specific MCG criteria applied to my case. I have included the relevant dates and records above for your review.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-05, though I understand my denial letter is the authoritative source for this deadline. I will submit this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I can also reach Molina through the member portal at molinahealthcare.com or by calling the Member Services number on my ID card.

Thank you for reviewing my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Riley Brooks
Member ID: W997409334
Date: [DATE OF SIGNING]
Contact phone: [PHONE NUMBER]
Contact address: [MAILING ADDRESS]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
